Call out exactly which lifecycle and reliability assumptions differ between local and remote transports and how your implementation enforces those differences.
content.suggested_opener: During a code review, you find no connection establishment/handshake for remote transport

content.authoring_prompt: Describe what will break if SDKs do not enforce protocol compliance with type safety across local and remote transport protocols. Specify concrete design requirements for serialization, prompts, and callbacks to adhere strictly to the shared protocol and its type contracts. Explain how each SDK and transport can validate and handle data consistently. Keep responses focused on protocol compliance and type safety.
content.suggested_opener: During a code review you find serialization ignores protocol compliance with type safety

content.authoring_prompt: Describe realistic interoperability failures that occur when SDKs or spec versions diverge in functionality or protocol features. Explain how ensuring all SDKs provide the same core functionality and full protocol support, and building MCP clients that can connect to any MCP server, prevents and recovers from those failures. Give concrete examples of cross-SDK mismatches and show how alignment of implementations reduces them.
content.suggested_opener: During a production incident, MCP clients fail due to SDK protocol mismatches.

content.authoring_prompt: Design and document a client implementation that keeps its cached view of available tools correct when the server declares the tools capability with "listChanged": true. Treat notifications/notifications/tools/list_changed as a hint, not as authoritative. Specify explicit discovery or polling and fallbacks such as periodic or manual refresh. Provide concise pseudo-code or algorithmic steps showing how the client re-checks the server's authoritative tool list and updates its cache.
content.suggested_opener: Server declared tools capability with listChanged true but emits few notifications.

content.authoring_prompt: You have a server exposing the Tools API but client discovery and notifications are failing. Ask the candidate to (a) explain why a server MUST declare the tools capability in its capabilities document, (b) provide the exact JSON snippet that declares tools with listChanged set to true, and (c) describe the operational problems that occur when the tools capability is omitted (clients unaware of tools or listChanged, missed or stale tool information).
content.suggested_opener: During a deployment, clients stop receiving listChanged notifications for tools.

content.authoring_prompt: You're designing a client UI for an application where an LLM may invoke tools. List concrete client-side controls and UI elements that implement the spec: make clear which tools are exposed to the AI model, insert visual indicators when tools are invoked, present confirmation prompts (with extra prompts for sensitive actions), show tool inputs before calling the server, validate tool results before passing them to the LLM, implement timeouts for tool calls, and log tool usage for audit. For each control, describe the user flow, the UI element shown, and how an operator can deny or review the invocation.
content.suggested_opener: During a code review, you notice AI tools exposed without confirmation prompts.

content.authoring_prompt: Write a brief implementation plan and concise pseudocode for an MCP client that treats the set of tools as dynamic. The client must call tools/list on demand and subscribe to notifications/tools/list_changed to learn about additions, removals, or updates at runtime. Show the exact call sequence you perform immediately before invoking any tool and how list_changed notifications update the client's authoritative view. In one short paragraph, explain how using on-demand listing together with list_changed prevents race conditions.
content.suggested_opener: A production agent must call tools/list and subscribe to notifications/tools/list_changed.

content.authoring_prompt: Write code or clear pseudocode that produces a tool result object representing a runtime error. Set isError to true and place human-readable error details inside the result's content array. Explain briefly why escalating tool errors as MCP protocol-level errors prevents the LLM from observing or handling them. Describe how the LLM could use the content array to decide remediation, retries, or human-in-the-loop actions.
content.suggested_opener: During testing, a tool emits a runtime error but escalates it to MCP protocol-level.

content.authoring_prompt: Implement a function that disambiguates tool names when aggregating tools from multiple MCP servers. The function should accept the tool name plus server metadata (user-defined server name and server URI) and return a unique tool identifier using one of the safe strategies: concatenating a user-defined server name, generating a random prefix, or using the server URI as a prefix. Do not rely on the initialization-provided name for uniqueness. Provide brief tests demonstrating each strategy and a 2-3 sentence rationale comparing their trade-offs.
content.suggested_opener: During integration, MCP servers expose tools with identical initialization-provided names.

content.authoring_prompt: Design and implement a UI approval gate that enforces explicit human-in-the-loop approval before any model-invoked tool executes. Define an audit log schema and retention policy that records approvals, invocations, denials, and related metadata for traceability. Provide API contracts and server-side invocation code that require approval tokens and never surface internal errors or diagnostics to clients. Include brief UI mockups, access-control rules, and example sanitization/error-handling snippets.
content.suggested_opener: During an integration, model-controlled tools require human-in-the-loop approval in UI.

content.authoring_prompt: Analyze the architectural tradeoffs between representing a resource with an https:// URI versus using another or a custom URI scheme and serving the resource contents through MCP. Explain the conditions under which servers SHOULD use https:// per the quoted guidance and when they SHOULD prefer another scheme. Describe the practical implementation implications: which party performs fetching and when the server must download or proxy contents via MCP. Keep the explanation concise and grounded in the provided guidance.
content.suggested_opener: An engineer asks whether to publish resources as https:// URIs or via MCP.

content.authoring_prompt: Provide implementation-level pseudocode or code snippets enforcing the documented security requirements. Validate all resource URIs (including file:// mappings) before any operation; properly encode binary data when returning contents (for example, base64 in a blob field); and perform permission checks before listing or returning contents. Show how to implement access controls for sensitive resources and include a resource annotation example with an audience array containing the valid values "user" and "assistant". For each MUST/SHOULD, add a one-line justification of where and why it is enforced.
content.suggested_opener: During a code review, you find file:// mappings exposed without URI validation.

content.authoring_prompt: Analyze the provided spec excerpt about resourceTemplates and the completion API. Identify what the excerpt explicitly states and which claims in the candidate answer are inferred rather than quoted. For each inferred recommendation (for example, “clients must expand templates themselves”), explain whether the excerpt justifies it and list alternative client behaviors that remain consistent with the spec. Support every conclusion by citing exact phrases or lines from the excerpt.
content.suggested_opener: A CI job logs a resources/templates/list response containing uriTemplate file:///{path}.

content.authoring_prompt: Require the candidate to implement server-side handling for a resources/read request that fails. They must show when to return JSON-RPC error -32002 versus -32603, and produce an error object with code -32002, a human-readable message (for example "Resource not found") and structured error.data containing the requested uri. Include the mandatory resource URI validation step and provide minimal pseudocode plus example JSON-RPC responses for both failure paths.
content.suggested_opener: A client issues a resources/read request for an unvalidated resource URI.

content.authoring_prompt: Provide examinees the quoted line: “Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications…”. Then present a student response that asserts specific protocol mechanics as requirements. Ask candidates to analyze whether the quoted text supports those specific mechanics, identifying each unsupported claim and explaining why. Require a concise model answer and a short rubric that grants full credit only if the respondent concludes the quote is a high-level analogy and cannot by itself justify the listed mechanics.
content.suggested_opener: Your team treats MCP like USB-C when connecting AI applications to systems.

content.authoring_prompt: Refer to the guidance: "Create MCP servers to expose your data and tools." Analyze why keeping the server role (exposing data and tools) distinct from the client role (consuming resources and orchestrating them) is recommended. Describe architectural tradeoffs and concrete implementation problems that arise if those roles are collapsed into a monolith, emphasizing the loss of the operational boundary between exposing resources and consuming/orchestrating them. Conclude with a prioritized list of the top three impacts.
content.suggested_opener: During a design review, MCP servers are being merged into a single monolith.

content.authoring_prompt: Explain why a client API exposes explicit capability flags that are set at construction time, as shown by ClientCapabilities.builder().roots(true).sampling().elicitation(). For each capability—filesystem roots support (with list-change notifications), LLM sampling support, and elicitation capability—analyze plausible implementation trade-offs and operational implications of enabling them. Base your analysis only on the concepts shown in the snippet and give concise, engineer-focused guidance for a design decision.
content.suggested_opener: Your team must decide whether to enable roots, sampling, and elicitation.

content.authoring_prompt: You are reviewing a transport configured with a custom HttpRequest.Builder that embeds a never-expiring token. Describe the security and operational risks of using a static HttpRequest.Builder and explain why it prevents per-request credential rotation. When dynamic authentication is needed, state the correct approach and name the interfaces to implement. Briefly explain at a high level how implementing McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer or McpAsyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer lets the transport adjust authentication at request time.
content.suggested_opener: A production incident shows transport always sends the same never-expiring token.

content.authoring_prompt: Using the roots capability, describe what breaks when client.addRoot or client.removeRoot is invoked without client.rootsListChangedNotification. Explain how the server's view of accessible filesystem roots becomes stale and why that can lead to incorrect or unsafe behavior. Give two concrete examples of failures or safety issues that could result and state the correct client-side notification sequence.
content.suggested_opener: During testing, addRoot and removeRoot calls occur without notification.

content.authoring_prompt: Describe the failure mode when the wrong HTTP request customizer type is registered for an MCP transport. Be explicit which interfaces the transport expects: McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer or McpAsyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer, and explain why the customizer type must match the MCP client type. State the resulting observable behavior on HTTP request modifications.
content.suggested_opener: During a code review you spot McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer used with async MCP client

content.authoring_prompt: Write a short implementation that ensures the client initializes the connection before calling any APIs. For a sync client show McpClient.sync(transport).build(); call client.initialize(); then call client.listTools(). For an async client describe the async initialize flow you would follow. In 2–4 sentences explain why initialize() is required (mention MCP session, protocol and capability negotiation, and change/notification consumers) and what may fail if it is skipped.
content.suggested_opener: During deployment, the McpSyncClient fails to call initialize() before listTools().
